title: I CAN'T GO TO SCHOOL – IT'S RAINING!
subtitle: For questions 1–8, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
passage:
It's true that a popular topic of conversation in England is the weather. Have you ever taken a day off school because of it? Would you [[0]] suspicious if someone didn't turn up for school because of the weather?

Well, in 1960s England, these were actually [[1]] reasons to miss school. Back then, teachers were required to record reasons why pupils weren't at school each day. This is clear from [[2]] at a log from Leighton Buzzard, in the county of Bedfordshire. [[3]], the reason for non-attendance was the weather.

Victorian school wasn't free. As such, poor people could attend, but only [[4]] they were [[5]] by charitable organisations. They didn't use to have appropriate clothing and wore scruffy, thin tops, dresses or trousers, [[6]] without coats or shoes. Deciding not to set [[7]] on foot to school in poor weather conditions suddenly becomes understandable. It must have been a real risk to their health. One day, when only 30% of the pupils went to class, lessons were [[8]] and everyone huddled together close to the fire.

items.explainCorrect: **Valid reasons** = acceptable / legitimate reasons (to miss school).

explainIfChosen.0: **Correct reasons** is awkward — *correct* fits answers, not excuses.
explainIfChosen.1: **True reasons** is not the natural collocation here.
explainIfChosen.3: **Proper reasons** is less idiomatic than *valid reasons*.

items.explainCorrect: **Looking at** a log = reading / checking it — fits *clear from looking at*.

explainIfChosen.2: **Examining at** is wrong (*examining a log* — no *at*).
explainIfChosen.3: **Studying at** is wrong (*studying a log* — no *at*).

items.explainCorrect: **Frequently** = often — weather was often the reason for absence.

explainIfChosen.2: **Almost** needs another word (*almost always*) — incomplete here.

items.explainCorrect: **Only if** — they could attend only on the condition that charity paid.
**Sponsored by** charities = financially supported so they could attend.

explainIfChosen.0: **Guaranteed by** does not mean paid for / supported.
explainIfChosen.2: **Donated by** usually applies to money/things, not people attending school.
explainIfChosen.3: **Commissioned by** means ordered to do work — wrong meaning.

items.explainCorrect: **Often without coats** = frequently barefoot / coatless — fits the hardship.

explainIfChosen.1: **Rarely** means almost never — opposite of the idea.

explainIfChosen.0: **Set in** means begin (of weather/mood) — wrong here.

items.explainCorrect: **Lessons were suspended** = temporarily stopped (because so few pupils came).

explainIfChosen.1: **Opposed** means against something — wrong for lessons.
explainIfChosen.2: **Excluded** means left out — not the usual collocation with *lessons*.
